title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Under HSAB reasoning, lanthanide ions prefer oxygen donors while borderline Ni(II) binds both nitrogen and oxygen, so multidentate N/O ligands are used to steer mixed-metal hydrolysis.
explanation: The authors use hard/soft acid-base preferences to explain why amino acids, Schiff bases, and amino polyols can control hydrolysis. They also note that coordination sites among Ln, 3d ions, and multidentate ligands are often unpredictable, so structures can form without a clear pattern.
scope: Ligand choice for 3d-4f clusters, especially Ni(II) with lanthanides.
caveats: HSAB is used as a design rationale; the same section stresses that coordination outcomes remain poorly predictable.
